correspondence.component_scope: Selected opening southeast of Barrocas into the Teofilândia headward corridor
correspondence.finding: The first eastward selected section follows the mapped intermittent Riacho Caroá drainage south/east of Barrocas, around the Milho Verde–Boi Preto–Ipueira rural setting. SEI Barrocas and the overlapping IBGE Teofilândia sheet depict its passage east of the Barrocas boundary and continuation toward Cabeça da Vaca. The latter sheet closes the municipal-sheet seam, rather than relying on the regional basin outline.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized headward-component scale
correspondence.name_scope: Upper mapped corridor only; no exact source-point or name-transition vertex asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Cabeça da Vaca water-body connection and upper turn toward Biritinga
correspondence.finding: IBGE Teofilândia depicts the connected Açude Cabeça da Vaca setting and river continuing east through Cabeça da Vaca, Lagoa do Ramo and Vargem de Baixo. The river then takes the southward turn shown along the western Biritinga setting, continuing past Morro da Onça, Ajudante and Mato Grosso toward Biritinga. SEI Biritinga labels the upper river Rio Cabeça da Vaca and its Cajueiro junction with Rio Dois Irmãos; SEI Barrocas independently supplies the upper Dois Irmãos/Inhambupe alternate boundary wording. The mapped connection is continuous even though the labels differ.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at generalized water-body and connector scale
correspondence.name_scope: Source-specific upper names and reservoir name retained separately; no whole-route synonym declaration.
correspondence.lake_reservoir_setting: The small Cabeça da Vaca impoundment is explicitly read in the connected upper corridor. The downstream Biritinga sheet also shows a small river widening south of the town; no additional reservoir name is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Biritinga to the upper Inhambupe municipal corridor
correspondence.finding: SEI Biritinga shows the selected southeast/east continuation south of Biritinga through Poço Grande, Bebedouro and Vila Nova. The Paracatu enters from the Patabia/Vila do Alto side; the selected line stays on the Inhambupe receiving corridor. It continues through Curral de Fora/Maracanã and the Pedras junction, then southeast toward Terra Vermelha, Terra Dura and Monte Alegre II. SEI Inhambupe depicts the Vitória junction and onward bend toward the Inhambupe town setting. CPRM independently supplies the same generalized river and side-tributary arrangement.
correspondence.correspondence: complete
correspondence.name_scope: Main receiving river only; tributary names remain bounded to their own branches.

correspondence.component_scope: Inhambupe town, Una-side junction and lower municipal floodplain
correspondence.finding: The selected line bends east/northeast and then southeast past Inhambupe, where the northward Una/Mulungu drainage joins the receiving river. SEI Inhambupe separates this from the selected western branch and depicts the downstream Ribeiro junction. Farther southeast the line enters the broad flood-prone river corridor around Ibatui and continues east toward Entre Rios. The original Esplanada 2007 northern sheet overlaps the eastern floodplain and its continuation toward Cardeal da Silva.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary river/floodplain-component scale
correspondence.lake_reservoir_setting: Floodplain and wet-ground symbols accompany the downstream river. Nearby small lakes, including the named group southwest of Inhambupe town, are not a selected through-lake chain; their presence is not used to reroute or rename the selected line.

correspondence.component_scope: Entre Rios–Cardeal da Silva–Esplanada lower river
correspondence.finding: The two original Esplanada 2007 sheets and the 2020 municipal map depict the selected east/southeast lower river through the Entre Rios/Cardeal da Silva setting, then past Gameleira, Boa Vista, Cachoeira, Água Boa/Água Branca and the Corte Grande–Palame setting. The mapped north-side tributaries remain separate, and the lower Bu junction is explicitly depicted before the terminal coastal reach. CPRM's Corte Grande hydrometric locality corroborates the lower corridor at regional scale.
correspondence.correspondence: complete
correspondence.lake_reservoir_setting: A river/floodplain passage rather than a large reservoir or lake chain. Side channels and smaller tributaries are retained as context without exact bank matching.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual selected terminal at Baixio
correspondence.finding: Both Esplanada editions follow the named river from the Palame/Bu-side setting through the final coastal meanders to Baixio. The historical 2007 sheet expressly marks Barra do Rio Inhambupe and shows the adjacent coastal strip, river-mouth continuation and coastal drainage; the 2020 map shows the same terminal corridor against the Atlantic coastline. This agrees with the actual selected downstream end at ordinary corridor scale, independently of the model's sea terminal class.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at generalized terminal-component scale
correspondence.terminal_setting: Atlantic coastal-mouth corridor at Baixio/Barra do Rio Inhambupe, Esplanada; no present-day precise opening-position claim.

correspondence.component_scope: northern headward pond-stream opening and westward-to-southward bend
correspondence.finding: Ryan1990 depicts the small-waterbody country south of the separately mapped Fraser valley, including the selected westward and then southward drainage sequence beside the divide. The selected opening is followed through that northern lake-and-stream setting into the south-southeast-running arm. The map distinguishes this arm from the Fraser corridor to its north and from adjoining western drainage.
correspondence.correspondence: observed at ordinary generalized headward/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: Regional cartography establishes the opening corridor and its downstream continuation, not an exact surveyed source pond or a name for the small feeder.

correspondence.component_scope: northern lake complex and southward inter-lake connectors
correspondence.finding: The detailed2003 original depicts the north-entering watercourse and the large irregular lake-and-channel complex in the eastern part of its sheet, followed by the southward chain of lakes and short river links. These correspond to the selected southeastward leg, its eastward lake crossing and subsequent southward sequence. Ryan1990 overlaps both ends and continues the chain beyond the detailed sheet's southern boundary.
correspondence.correspondence: observed
correspondence.limits: No individual northern lake hydronyms are established. The detailed sheet covers an intermediate part of the selected route, not its northernmost source or coastal terminal.

correspondence.component_scope: southern continuation of the northern feeder and junction with the eastward valley
correspondence.finding: Ryan1990 carries the connected southern lake sequence down to the eastward valley and labels the continuing Kogaluk River. Anderson Figure108 separately draws the long northern arm entering the upper system and the western upper branches. The selected path then stays on the long eastward corridor rather than taking the southern Mistastin drainage.
correspondence.correspondence: observed at ordinary corridor scale
correspondence.limits: The Kogaluk label on the continuing valley is not extended backward as an established local name for every feeder segment. No exact tributary-number boundary is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: named Kogaluk valley, incoming Mistastin River and Cabot Lake passage
correspondence.finding: Ryan1990 and Wheeler1980 show the eastward Kogaluk river corridor, a substantial tributary arriving from the south just upstream of the long narrow Cabot Lake, and the main route through that lake and out its eastern end. Ryan labels the southern tributary Mistastin River; Anderson Figure108 and its account independently link that tributary to Mistastin Lake. The selected route continues from the west through Cabot Lake and does not enter the southern tributary.
correspondence.correspondence: observed

correspondence.component_scope: lower eastward river and actual coastal terminal
correspondence.finding: Ryan1990 follows the lower river eastward beyond Cabot Lake, through the lower valley, and then northward past a mapped falls to the southern shore of Voisey Bay. It separately depicts the neighboring parallel valley and coastal inlets. Anderson's original Figure108 also carries the river to its labeled Voisey Bay mouth, and its prose describes the river's southern-bay outlet. These observations cover the selected actual receiving-water setting beyond the river's long eastward reach.
correspondence.correspondence: observed
correspondence.limits: The findings do not equate the retained model endpoint with an exact modern mouth or shoreline vertex.

correspondence.component_scope: Initial southeastern small-lake and stream headward setting
correspondence.finding: The selected headward end lies in the small-lake landscape north of Washburn Lake. The original shows the associated west/northwest stream corridor, small contributing lakes and some intermittent-stream symbols. The selected route then turns north. No hydronym was established for this initial feeder.
correspondence.correspondence: Small-lake/stream component correspondence at ordinary generalized scale; not a claim that every short modeled line is a mapped perennial channel.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward elongate-lake corridor and material western turn
correspondence.finding: The original maps the distinctive northward chain of narrow elongate waterbodies and connecting channels. At its northern end the route joins the larger west-flowing corridor with a separate eastern arrival, then turns west/northwest through the lowland stream setting.
correspondence.correspondence: The lake-chain connection and material junction were read on original pixels, rather than inferred only from model connectivity.

correspondence.component_scope: Western lower feeder and southeastern Namaycush inlet
correspondence.finding: The selected lower feeder bends west across the sheet boundary and reaches the southeastern part of Namaycush Lake through the mapped broad, locally divided inlet corridor. It is distinct from the separate incoming river at the lake’s western side.
correspondence.correspondence: Ordinary corridor continuity across the two original sheets established; precise braided-channel selection is outside scope.

correspondence.component_scope: Namaycush Lake passage and Nanook outlet
correspondence.finding: The selected route crosses Namaycush Lake and follows its northward/northeast outlet. Nanook River is explicitly printed along that outlet. The separate western river approach is visible but is not the selected headward arm.
correspondence.correspondence: The actual receiving lake and downstream outlet are established. The lake retains its own name and is not assigned the river hydronym.

correspondence.component_scope: Nanook middle corridor across the northern sheet boundary
correspondence.finding: The Nanook-labelled route continues north/northeast through elongate waterbodies and intervening channels. The southern Burns Lake sheet and western Cape Stang sheet jointly show the continuation, nearby side-lake arrivals and the eastward sheet-edge transition.
correspondence.correspondence: Named river-system continuation and material connectors established at corridor scale; no transfer of the name to every waterbody.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower junctions and broad terminal lake approach
correspondence.finding: The main mapped channel bends north through the lower lake chain, with separate southeastern tributary/lake connections and an eastern incoming lake branch, and reaches the broad unnamed lower lake. The selected route takes this main lower-lake passage rather than any of the eastward tributary routes.
correspondence.correspondence: Major incoming branches and the selected lower-lake continuation distinguished. Individual side-branch names are not required or assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Northeast lake outlet and actual coastal terminal
correspondence.finding: The broad lower lake discharges through its northeast outlet into the final north-leading river channel, which reaches the southern head of Hadley Bay. The eastern lake arrivals and nearby separate coastal stream mouths remain distinct. The selected terminal corresponds to this Nanook-system outlet into the bay.
correspondence.correspondence: Actual terminal waterbody and final channel established from original cartography; coastal prose supplies only broader bay context.

correspondence.component_scope: Far-northern head near La Angélica and the Laprida–Coronel Rodolfo Bunge corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected head lies among mapped small depressions and marshes in the La Angélica–La Eladia country. It proceeds south through the La Elena setting and across the principal transport corridor west of Coronel Rodolfo Bunge. The original detailed map shows local drainage marks and separate waterlogged depressions, but does not establish an integrated named or unnamed waterway carrying this entire selected northern chain southward.
correspondence.correspondence: Original landscape and local drainage coverage; complete selected receiving connection unresolved.

correspondence.component_scope: El Rosario–La Choza–Coleu Huincul and Juan E. Barra headward transition
correspondence.finding: The selected route bends southwest past El Rosario, El Sol Argentino and La Choza, through the Coleu Huincul setting northwest of Mariano Roldán, and then toward the country west of Juan E. Barra. The maps distinguish this lowland from Laguna La Salada, La Golondrina, El Vigilante and El Balde farther east. A separately depicted Quequén headward branch approaches through the western lowland, with the labels Arroyo Quequén and Brazo del Arroyo Quequén visible on the national maps. Its proximity and eventual receiving setting do not establish the full selected northern connector.
correspondence.correspondence: Original geographic coverage read; upstream integration remains the primary material gap.

correspondence.component_scope: El Recuerdo–La Libertad–Los Tres Reyes and the straightened upper receiving reach
correspondence.finding: At El Recuerdo–La Libertad the selected route reaches the mapped upper receiving valley and continues south along the narrow, conspicuously straightened channel past San Pedro and west of La Araucarita/La Sortija. Laguna Los Tres Reyes lies to the east of this selected passage; the route is not a traversal of the lake's principal mapped basin. Western drains and short feeders enter the receiving corridor. The original 1:250,000 map supplies continuous coverage across the missing central sheet area in the detailed 1:100,000 mosaic.
correspondence.correspondence: Original channel, drainage and adjacent-lake correspondence. No date, construction history or present hydraulic operating condition of the straightening is inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle receiving junctions near El Quemún and the southward valley
correspondence.finding: The straight upper corridor bends southwest into the junction country near El Charabón, Santa María and Almacén El Quemún, where the original map depicts several western tributary approaches entering the river. The selected valley then continues south through Los Toldos and El Campito, west of the separate La Ida lakes, and crosses the principal east–west road. The field-based 2009 article's already-read prose independently identifies Pillahuincó Grande as a tributary of Quequén Salado; it does not by itself assign that name to an exact map junction or to the selected mainstem.
correspondence.correspondence: Original connected main valley and material tributary junctions; detailed tributary names remain unassigned where not legible on the bounded original.

correspondence.component_scope: La Josefina–San Graciano–Micaela Cascallares receiving river
correspondence.finding: South of the road crossing, the original river winds through La Providencia and La Josefina and bends southeast past San Graciano and La Pampa de las Avestruces toward the rail corridor west of Micaela Cascallares. The Quequén Salado name is printed along this connected river. Lateral drainage and wetland areas are visible, while the selected course stays in the principal incised valley rather than entering the separate surrounding lakes.
correspondence.correspondence: Original named-river corridor, valley bends and crossings; map-boundary details covered by the continuous 1:250,000 original.

correspondence.component_scope: Irene–Route 3–Indio Rico junction and Oriente–Copetonas
correspondence.finding: The river crosses the railway east of Irene, passes La Paquita and the La Paloma/La Rosa crossing of Route 3, and continues south. Arroyo Indio Rico is separately labeled on the western approach and joins the selected receiving valley downstream of that highway. The main river then passes the San Pedro setting between Oriente and Copetonas and crosses their connecting transport corridor. Indio Rico remains a tributary identity, not a name for this selected mainstem.
correspondence.correspondence: Original lower-river and actual tributary receiving-junction correspondence; article prose supplies limited independent tributary context.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Quequén Salado through the coastal dunes to the actual terminal
correspondence.finding: Below Oriente–Copetonas, the selected main valley continues south past El Chajá, Arúa, Santa María and El Rincón de San Pedro, through the coastal dune belt. The original 1:250,000 map shows the river widening and curving beside Balneario Oriente before opening into Mar Argentino/Océano Atlántico Sur. The actual terminal is this river mouth. It is separate from the coastal La Blanca/La Salada lake country to the west and from the Arroyo Claromecó system to the east.
correspondence.correspondence: Continuous original lower-river, dune crossing and ocean receiving connection; no exact contemporary mouth position inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected component scope, wetland and storage limits
correspondence.finding: The retained object comprises one selected mainstem FID. The original maps show a low-gradient depression-rich upper landscape, a straightened receiving reach, tributary junctions and a confined lower river. No large in-stream lake or reservoir traversal is depicted along the established downstream selected corridor. Nearby named lakes and off-route wetland basins are not treated as through-flow components merely because they lie in the surrounding catchment.
correspondence.correspondence: Original cartographic component reading; publisher abstract supplies only broad low-gradient and flooding context.
